answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can enforce max-flow trust bounds from verified seeds. Nodes route validation credit across interaction edges, limiting influence to a bounded trust horizon. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of establishing authentic links from honest peers, preventing a hostile gale of forged identities from gaining consensus weight. However, this topology penalizes honest newcomers without connections and degrades when an erratic tide of churn fragments the graph.
